title: J1939 Data Link Erratic
shortDescription: Intermittent CAN bus communication loss between vehicle modules.
fullDescription:
SPN 639 is the SAE J1939 primary data link shared by engine ECM, transmission, ABS, body controller, and instrument cluster on Kenworth T680/T880/W990 trucks. FMI 2 means erratic/intermittent/incorrect data — packets are being received but not at expected content/rate.

Kenworth's shared platform with Peterbilt (both PACCAR) uses common failure points in the chassis harness, especially at the firewall pass-through and 9-pin diagnostic port. Corrosion at the battery junction box is another high-frequency cause. Symptoms range from flickering gauges to intermittent derate and transmission harsh shifting.

Always inspect grounds and backbone connectors before condemning a module.

fixSteps.title: Check grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect and clean battery negative, engine block ground, and cab ground straps. Torque to spec.

fixSteps.title: Measure CAN termination
fixSteps.instruction: Key off, measure CAN H to CAN L at 9-pin: should be ~60Ω.

fixSteps.title: Inspect firewall harness
fixSteps.instruction: Pull firewall pass-through connector, inspect and clean pins with contact cleaner. Apply dielectric grease.

whenToCallPro: If bus-off condition persists — PACCAR dealer diagnosis.
videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 SPN 639 FMI 2 J1939 CAN fault

faq.a: Gauges rely on J1939 data — intermittent bus = intermittent gauges.
Less than 10% of cases. Grounds and connectors first.

title: Engine Protection Derate Active
shortDescription: ECM commanded power reduction based on another critical parameter — secondary code to investigate.
fullDescription:
SPN 1569 FMI 31 is a 'downstream' code indicating the engine is currently derated as a protective response to a separate primary fault — usually low oil pressure, high coolant temp, or DEF system issues. FMI 31 means 'condition exists' rather than a specific sensor fault.

On Kenworth T680/T880 with PACCAR MX-11/MX-13 or Cummins ISX engines, this code never stands alone — always look for the companion root-cause code (SPN 100 for oil, SPN 110 for coolant, SPN 3610/3364 for DEF). Fixing the primary code clears 1569 automatically.

Ignoring the derate and continuing under load risks escalation to engine shutdown or catastrophic engine damage.

fixSteps.title: Pull full code list
fixSteps.instruction: Connect PACCAR Electronic Service Analyst (ESA) or JPro. Record ALL active codes. SPN 1569 is always secondary.

fixSteps.title: Address primary code
fixSteps.instruction: Repair the primary fault (oil, coolant, DEF, etc.). SPN 1569 will clear automatically once condition resolves.

fixSteps.title: Verify clear
fixSteps.instruction: After repair, run truck through a drive cycle. Rescan to confirm 1569 is inactive and no inducement remains.

whenToCallPro: If primary code is internal engine or aftertreatment — PACCAR dealer.
videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 SPN 1569 FMI 31 engine derate diagnose

faq.q: Why is my truck derated with no obvious fault?
faq.a: There IS a primary fault — scan with a proper tool, not just a cheap code reader.
Clearing without fixing root cause causes it to return within minutes under load.

title: DEF Tank Level Very Low (Severe)
shortDescription: DEF tank is essentially empty — 5 mph derate imminent or active.
fullDescription:
SPN 1761 FMI 1 indicates the DEF tank level is below the most-severe threshold. On Kenworth T680/T880, this triggers full EPA inducement: first a power derate (~25%), then 5 mph limp-home until DEF is refilled and the key is cycled.

Always refill with API-certified DEF (32.5% urea solution). Never substitute water, washer fluid, or non-certified additives — these destroy the SCR catalyst and cause multi-thousand-dollar damage.

If the gauge shows DEF present but this code is active, suspect frozen fluid around the level float (DEF freezes at 12°F / -11°C) or a failed DEF tank header sensor assembly.

fixSteps.title: Refill DEF
fixSteps.instruction: Add at least 2 gallons API-certified DEF. Cycle key off 30 sec, then start and drive above 5 mph.

fixSteps.title: Thaw if frozen
fixSteps.instruction: If ambient below 12°F and gauge still reads 0, park indoors or use engine heat — heated DEF line will thaw as engine warms.

fixSteps.title: Replace DEF header if faulty
fixSteps.instruction: Drain DEF, remove retaining ring, swap header assembly, refill.

whenToCallPro: If header fault or SCR derate persists after refill — PACCAR dealer.
videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 DEF empty 5 mph derate SPN 1761

faq.q: Can I tape over the DEF sensor wire?
faq.a: No — EPA tampering $5,000+ fine, and the truck still derates via NOx sensors.

faq.q: How far does DEF get me?
faq.a: DEF consumes ~2-3% of diesel gallons. A full 13-gallon DEF tank covers ~4,500 miles.

title: EGR Valve Not Responding Properly
shortDescription: Exhaust gas recirculation valve not moving to commanded position — stuck or sooted.
fullDescription:
SPN 2791 FMI 7 indicates the EGR valve is not reaching its commanded position. On Kenworth T680/T880 with PACCAR MX-11/MX-13, the EGR valve cycles soot-laden exhaust back to the intake — over time carbon deposits bind the valve shaft.

This code is commonly paired with poor fuel economy, black smoke, and power loss. Cleaning is often possible, but advanced cases require valve replacement. The EGR cooler is a companion component that can also fail — internal coolant leaks trigger SPN 110 overheating codes simultaneously.

Be aware: EGR components can exceed 500°F during operation — allow extended cooldown before service.

fixSteps.title: Clean EGR valve
fixSteps.instruction: Allow engine to cool. Remove EGR valve, clean carbon from shaft and sealing face with CRC intake cleaner and brass brush.

fixSteps.title: Actuation test
fixSteps.instruction: Reconnect and command EGR 0-100% via PACCAR ESA. Watch actual vs commanded. If sluggish, replace valve.

fixSteps.title: Replace EGR valve
fixSteps.instruction: Install new EGR valve with new gasket. Torque to spec. Perform calibration routine in ESA.

whenToCallPro: If cooler leak suspected or calibration required — dealer.
videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 PACCAR MX EGR valve clean SPN 2791

faq.a: EPA violation $5,000+ fine, plus modern tuning won't run without EGR.
Every 300,000-500,000 miles depending on duty cycle.

title: DPF Soot Load Critical — Regen Inhibited
shortDescription: DPF soot at critical level and regen cannot initiate — manual dealer service required.
fullDescription:
SPN 3719 FMI 0 means DPF soot load is at the most severe threshold. Automatic and parked regens are inhibited because conditions are unsafe or would not complete. The truck enters 5 mph derate.

On Kenworth T680/T880, this occurs when soot load exceeds ~150% — the regen would generate excessive exhaust temperatures and potentially damage the DPF substrate. A forced regen via PACCAR ESA at a dealer is typically the next step, or DPF removal for off-vehicle cleaning/baking.

If the DPF substrate has cracked from an uncontrolled burn or thermal event, replacement ($4,500+) is the only option.

causes.cause: Failed dosing system (cannot raise exhaust temp)

fixSteps.title: Tow to dealer
fixSteps.instruction: 5 mph derate — tow to PACCAR dealer with ESA capability for forced regen diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Forced regen or DPF removal
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer attempts a service-mode forced regen. If fails, DPF is removed for thermal/pneumatic cleaning at certified facility.

fixSteps.title: Replace if cracked
fixSteps.instruction: If substrate cracked, replace DPF assembly. New DPF $4,500-$6,000.

whenToCallPro: Always — dealer or certified aftertreatment shop.
videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 SPN 3719 FMI 0 DPF critical forced regen

faq.a: Not with FMI 0 — service-mode only, requires ESA and dealer authorization.
Avoid excessive idle, run highway miles weekly, change fuel and CCV filters on schedule.

title: DEF Pressure Low (Dosing System)
shortDescription: DEF supply module pressure below threshold — doser/pump/filter fault.
fullDescription:
SPN 4094 FMI 18 monitors DEF supply module output pressure during dosing. Low pressure means the DEF pump cannot build adequate pressure, a filter is clogged, or a supply line is restricted.

On Kenworth T680/T880, the DEF supply module (pump/heater/filter combo) is mounted near the tank. Common failures include plugged internal filter (replaceable), crystallized urea in the pump, or frozen lines in cold weather. If pressure cannot be built, SCR dosing stops and NOx conversion efficiency codes (SPN 4364) follow.

Always use fresh API-certified DEF. Contaminated or expired DEF clogs pump filters within months.

fixSteps.title: Check DEF lines for freeze
fixSteps.instruction: If below 12°F and truck sat overnight, wait for engine to warm and heated lines to thaw (15-30 min run time).

fixSteps.title: Replace DEF pump filter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove filter cap on DEF supply module, extract filter cartridge, install new. Prime system via ESA.

fixSteps.title: Replace DEF pump if still low pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and replace supply module. Re-prime and test pressure build via ESA.

whenToCallPro: If full supply module replacement — dealer pricing.
videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 DEF pump SPN 4094 filter replace

faq.q: When should DEF pump filter be replaced?
faq.a: Every 300,000 miles per PACCAR maintenance schedule, or at any 4094 code.
DEF freezes at 12°F. Heated lines thaw it but cold-start grace period is 20 min.

title: Aftertreatment SCR Inducement Severity 1
shortDescription: First-stage SCR inducement — persistent DEF or NOx fault causing derate countdown.
fullDescription:
SPN 5246 represents the aftertreatment SCR inducement counter. FMI 15 is the first severity stage — amber warnings active, with cascading derate over subsequent drive cycles if root cause isn't addressed.

On Kenworth T680/T880, SPN 5246 is always a companion code — the primary fault (SCR efficiency, DEF quality, dosing pressure, NOx sensor) sets first and 5246 tracks the EPA-mandated inducement timeline. Clearing 5246 alone does nothing; root cause must be fixed.

The 5-stage inducement progresses: amber CEL → solid amber → red lamp → derate → 5 mph limp home. Each stage typically spans 1-4 hours of operation depending on fault type.

fixSteps.title: Pull all active codes
fixSteps.instruction: With ESA, identify primary SCR-related fault driving the inducement.

fixSteps.title: Repair primary fault
fixSteps.instruction: Address DEF system, NOx sensor, or SCR catalyst issue per the root-cause SPN procedure.

fixSteps.title: Inducement reset
fixSteps.instruction: After repair, a drive cycle typically resets inducement. Dealer ESA can force reset if required.

videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 SPN 5246 SCR inducement diagnose

faq.q: Why is my truck warning me but running fine?
faq.a: Inducement is EPA-mandated escalation — running fine now doesn't mean it will be in 4 hours.
Inducement resets after primary fault clears and a drive cycle completes.

title: Coolant Temp High — Moderate Severity
shortDescription: Coolant temperature elevated above normal but below shutdown threshold.
fullDescription:
SPN 110 FMI 16 on Kenworth T680/T880 flags coolant temp between the warning and shutdown thresholds (typically 221-235°F / 105-113°C). The ECM derates power to prevent escalation to FMI 0 (severe) or FMI 31 (shutdown).

Common causes on PACCAR MX engines include clogged radiator fins, failed viscous fan clutch, low coolant, or stuck thermostat. A gradual rise under load typically indicates airflow/cooling capacity issue; rapid rise suggests head gasket or internal leak.

Pull over, let cool, and diagnose before continuing. Continued loading causes head gasket failure or cylinder head warpage.

fixSteps.title: Safe cooldown
fixSteps.instruction: Pull over, idle 2-3 min, then shut down. Wait 30+ min before opening hood. Never open cap hot.

fixSteps.title: Inspect and clean
fixSteps.instruction: Rinse radiator/CAC fins with low-pressure water. Check coolant level in surge tank. Look for external leaks.

fixSteps.title: Test fan and thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: Command fan on with ESA — should lock audibly. If not, replace viscous clutch. Thermostat test: feel upper radiator hose during warmup.

whenToCallPro: If head gasket or water pump failure — dealer.
videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 PACCAR MX overheat SPN 110 FMI 16

faq.a: Over 225°F is the danger zone. Over 240°F is head gasket territory.

faq.q: Why does it overheat on hills?
faq.a: Loaded climbs add heat faster than cooling can remove. Clean fins and check fan first.

title: Boost Pressure Below Normal — Least Severe
shortDescription: Intake boost below expected — mild CAC leak or VGT sluggish.
fullDescription:
SPN 102 FMI 17 is the least-severe low-boost code on Kenworth T680/T880 with PACCAR MX-11/MX-13. A mild boost shortfall — often an early-warning sign of a developing CAC leak, loose boot, or early VGT fouling.

Fuel economy typically drops 0.3-0.8 mpg as the ECM compensates with extra fuel. Smoke test the charge-air side first; most cases are a split end-tank on the CAC or a clamp that backed off.

If sealed, inspect VGT actuator for sticking. Commercial MX engines accumulate carbon on VGT vanes over 300,000+ miles.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test CAC
fixSteps.instruction: Pressurize charge-air with smoke machine. Look for leaks at boots, clamps, CAC tanks.

fixSteps.title: Tighten or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Re-torque T-bolt clamps or replace cracked CAC / split boot.

fixSteps.title: VGT test
fixSteps.instruction: With ESA, command VGT 0-100% and confirm actual tracks. If slow, remove turbo for vane cleaning.

videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 boost leak smoke test SPN 102

faq.a: Yes — but fuel economy suffers and black smoke sooted the DPF.
Shop smoke machine. Soap spray works too but misses small leaks.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Critical Low
shortDescription: Oil pressure below critical shutdown threshold — engine damage imminent.
fullDescription:
SPN 100 FMI 1 is the most severe oil-pressure code on Kenworth T680/T880 with PACCAR MX or Cummins ISX. The ECM triggers immediate engine protection shutdown timer — typically 30-60 seconds before engine stops.

If this code sets, STOP DRIVING. Continued operation in 30 seconds can destroy $25,000+ of main bearings, piston skirts, and cylinder liners. Common causes: catastrophic low oil (blown hose, drain plug out), failed oil pump, broken pickup tube, or spun bearing already in progress.

Shut down immediately and check oil level before attempting to restart. If level is fine, do not restart — tow to service.

fixSteps.title: STOP immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Pull safely off road and shut down engine. Do not attempt to restart until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Check oil and leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Look under truck for oil puddle. Pull dipstick — if dry, major external leak. If full, internal failure likely.

fixSteps.title: Tow to dealer
fixSteps.instruction: If internal failure suspected or level unchanged, tow to PACCAR dealer. Do not restart — damage is progressive.

videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 SPN 100 FMI 1 low oil pressure shutdown

faq.q: Can I drive to the next exit?
faq.a: NO. 30 seconds can destroy the engine. Pull over now.

faq.q: What if oil level is full?
faq.a: Internal failure — oil pump, bearing, or pickup. Tow, do not restart.

title: EGR Differential Pressure Above Normal
shortDescription: EGR delta-pressure sensor reads higher than expected — sooted venturi or stuck EGR.
fullDescription:
SPN 411 FMI 0 on Kenworth T680/T880 indicates the ECM sees excessive pressure drop across the EGR metering venturi. Usually means the EGR system is heavily sooted, restricting flow, or the delta-pressure sensor sample lines are plugged.

This often pairs with power loss, black smoke, and SCR efficiency codes as combustion temperatures and NOx targets drift. Routine EGR cleaning (every 300,000-500,000 miles on PACCAR MX) prevents escalation.

Work hot-side EGR components only after extended cooldown — EGR cooler surfaces exceed 500°F.

fixSteps.title: Clean DP sample lines
fixSteps.instruction: Remove small metal tubes from EGR DP sensor and venturi. Blow out with compressed air — often carbon plugs cause false high readings.

fixSteps.title: Clean EGR components
fixSteps.instruction: Remove EGR valve and venturi. Clean carbon with brass brush and intake cleaner. Reinstall with new gaskets.

fixSteps.title: Replace components if damaged
fixSteps.instruction: If venturi warped or valve seized, replace assembly.

whenToCallPro: If EGR cooler replacement needed — dealer.
videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 PACCAR MX EGR DP sensor SPN 411

faq.q: Can soot really block sensor tubes?
faq.a: Yes — hairline restrictions cause false high-DP readings all the time.
Every 300,000-500,000 miles based on PACCAR recommendation.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage High
shortDescription: Rail pressure sensor reads above normal — circuit open or sensor fault.
fullDescription:
SPN 157 FMI 3 indicates the fuel rail pressure sensor signal is above the expected maximum, typically from an open ground, open signal wire, or failed sensor. On Kenworth T680/T880 with PACCAR MX or Cummins ISX common rail, the rail operates at 25,000-32,000 PSI — a pressure capable of skin injection injury.

Never loosen fuel lines on a running engine. Always wait 10+ minutes after shutdown for rail pressure to bleed down before servicing.

Diagnose sensor harness first — pin corrosion or chafed wires against the engine are most common. A true out-of-range pressure reading can also set this code if the pressure regulator fails closed (rare).

fixSteps.title: SAFETY — bleed pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off key and wait 10+ min for rail to depressurize. Never work on common rail with engine running.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Key on, back-probe 5V reference, ground, and signal. Missing reference/ground points to harness. Signal above 4.8V with rail empty = sensor failure.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clean sensor boss before removal. Install new sensor with proper torque. Clear codes with ESA.

videoSearchQuery: Kenworth T680 SPN 157 FMI 3 rail pressure sensor

faq.a: Yes — common rail diesel at 30,000 PSI pierces skin invisibly, causes gangrene, amputation risk. ER immediately if exposed.
Sensor — 70%+ of 157 codes. HPFP is last resort.
